items.t: Said the federal tariffs are illegal and that he is going to court over them.
items.q: They’re illegal, and they’re making things harder for North Carolinians who are working around the clock to keep the lights on, pay rent, and afford gas. We’re going to court to protect our state.

items.t: Said it is unlawful and unconstitutional for the Department of Education to withhold money that Congress has appropriated.
items.q: It’s unlawful and unconstitutional for the Department of Education to withhold money that Congress has appropriated. I’m going to court to get this money for our students, our schools, and North Carolina families.

items.t: Said critical race theory is not happening and does not exist.
items.q: It's literally not happening, ma'am," Jackson said. "It's not about whether we're against it or for it, it's about a party that's convinced people it's a threat, but it doesn't exist.

items.t: Said the drafting of racial curriculum should be left to local education officials.
items.q: At a July forum in Holly Springs, the state legislator told a voter that the drafting of racial curriculum should be left to local education officials.

items.t: Said he voted for the TikTok bill because he believes the chance of a ban is practically zero.
items.q: the reason I voted for it was because I genuinely believe the chance of a ban is practically zero for a lot of reasons – financial, political, geopolitical – I just don't think there's any real chance of a ban.

items.t: Said people should be able to trust that the price they see on shelves is the price they will pay.
